## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-4-cell-type-identification/>

Part 2 of 3. Three automated annotation approaches are run on the object saved
by part 1:

- **SingleR**: reference-based (correlation to labelled reference profiles); the
  article uses `MonacoImmuneData` for PBMCs (HPCA is broad, DICE is less
  granular).
- **scType**: marker-based gene set scoring per cluster.
- **scCATCH**: tissue-specific marker database matching per cluster.

No single method is authoritative. Part 3 compares them.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 9-14). Changes made
for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter,
paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or
`FIX:` in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}

# Core single-cell analysis
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)

# Automated annotation methods
library(SingleR)
library(BiocParallel) # speed up SingleR
library(celldex)
library(scCATCH)

# Data structures
library(SingleCellExperiment)

# Marker processing
library(HGNChelper)
library(openxlsx) # reads the scType database

# Visualization and data manipulation
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)

source(here::here("helper_functions", "params_read.R"))
params <- params_ingest()

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
integr.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$integr.dir)
annot.dir <- file.path(integr.dir, params$annot.subdir)

# Create output directories
for (d in c("plots", "plots/automated_annotation", "annotations")) {
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(annot.dir, d))) dir.create(file.path(annot.dir, d), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Configure plotting defaults
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

cluster.col <- params$cluster.col

# Files from part 1 and for part 3
annotated_part1.file <- "merged_integrated_clustered_manual_annotated.rds"
annotated_part2.file <- "merged_integrated_clustered_manual_auto_annotated.rds"

if (params$species != "human") {
  warning("SingleR references and scType/scCATCH databases below are set up for human data; review before using species = '", params$species, "'")
}
```

## Load object from part 1

```{r step2_load_obj}

integrated_seurat <- readRDS(file.path(integr.dir, annotated_part1.file))
load(file.path(annot.dir, "annotations", "annot_part1.RData")) # umap_reduction, cluster_to_celltype objects

DefaultAssay(integrated_seurat) <- "RNA"
Idents(integrated_seurat) <- cluster.col
cat("Cells:", ncol(integrated_seurat), " UMAP reduction:", umap_reduction, "\n")
```

## SingleR: reference-based annotation

SingleR compares the expression of each cell with labelled reference profiles
and assigns the best-correlated label. It cannot assign a type that is absent
from the reference.

### Test multiple references

HumanPrimaryCellAtlas (Broad), MonacoImmuneData (immune-specific), DatabaseImmuneCellExpression (DICE)

```{r step3_singler, message = TRUE, warning = FALSE}

# Convert Seurat to SingleCellExperiment for SingleR
sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(integrated_seurat)

# Layers may be on-disk BPCells matrices, which DelayedArray (used inside
# SingleR) cannot wrap; pull the log-normalized data into memory as a dgCMatrix.
# Only logcounts is needed, so drop the other assays to save memory.
sce <- SingleCellExperiment::SingleCellExperiment(
  assays = list(logcounts = as(SummarizedExperiment::assay(sce, "logcounts"), "dgCMatrix")),
  colData = SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)
)

## Set up BiocParallel for use with SingleR
# Ubuntu / Linux optimized parameters
# availableCores() respects cgroup/SLURM limits; detectCores() does not
n_workers <- max(1L, parallelly::availableCores() - 2L)

bp <- MulticoreParam(workers = n_workers, progressbar = TRUE, RNGseed = 1234)

# Reference 1: HumanPrimaryCellAtlas (Broad)
hpca_ref <- celldex::HumanPrimaryCellAtlasData()

singler_hpca <- SingleR(
  test = sce,
  ref = hpca_ref,
  labels = hpca_ref$label.main,
  assay.type.test = "logcounts",
  BPPARAM = bp
)

integrated_seurat$singler_hpca <- singler_hpca$labels

# Reference 2: MonacoImmuneData (Immune-Specific)
monaco_ref <- celldex::MonacoImmuneData()

singler_monaco <- SingleR(
  test = sce,
  ref = monaco_ref,
  labels = monaco_ref$label.main,
  assay.type.test = "logcounts",
  BPPARAM = bp
)

integrated_seurat$singler_monaco <- singler_monaco$labels

# Reference 3: DatabaseImmuneCellExpression (dice)
dice_ref <- celldex::DatabaseImmuneCellExpressionData()

singler_dice <- SingleR(
  test = sce,
  ref = dice_ref,
  labels = dice_ref$label.main,
  assay.type.test = "logcounts",
  BPPARAM = bp
)

integrated_seurat$singler_dice <- singler_dice$labels
```

### Compare references

Include the previous manual annotation for comparison.

```{r step4_singler_compare, fig.width = 16, fig.height = 12}

# Visualize all three references
p_hpca <- DimPlot(integrated_seurat, reduction = umap_reduction,
                  group.by = "singler_hpca", pt.size = 0.1) +
  labs(title = "HPCA Reference") +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7))

p_monaco <- DimPlot(integrated_seurat, reduction = umap_reduction,
                    group.by = "singler_monaco", pt.size = 0.1) +
  labs(title = "Monaco Reference") +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7))

p_dice <- DimPlot(integrated_seurat, reduction = umap_reduction,
                  group.by = "singler_dice", pt.size = 0.1) +
  labs(title = "DICE Reference") +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7))

p_manual_ref <- DimPlot(integrated_seurat, reduction = umap_reduction,
                        group.by = "manual_annotation", pt.size = 0.1) +
  labs(title = "Manual") +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7))

p_ref_comparison <- (p_manual_ref | p_hpca) / (p_monaco | p_dice)
print(p_ref_comparison)

ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/automated_annotation/10_singler_reference_comparison.png"),
       p_ref_comparison, width = 16, height = 12, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

### Choose primary SingleR annotation method

```{r step4b_singler_choose, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}
# For this tutorial, we'll use Monaco as the primary SingleR annotation
# (reference chosen by params$singler.ref)
stopifnot(params$singler.ref %in% c("hpca", "monaco", "dice"))
integrated_seurat$singler_annotation <-
  integrated_seurat@meta.data[[paste0("singler_", params$singler.ref)]]

# Visualize chosen reference
p_singler_final <- DimPlot(
  integrated_seurat,
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  group.by = "singler_annotation",
  label = TRUE,
  label.size = 3,
  pt.size = 0.1,
  repel = TRUE
) +
  ggtitle(paste0("SingleR Annotation (", params$singler.ref, " Reference)")) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
print(p_singler_final)

ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/automated_annotation/11_singler_final_annotation.png"),
       p_singler_final, width = 11, height = 8, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## scType: marker-based gene set scoring

Each cell's scaled expression is scored against positive (and negative) marker
sets for each cell type in the database, scores are summed per cluster, and
each cluster takes its top-scoring type.

Source and database files are downloaded from GitHub, but versions available on 2026-10-26 are available in the `scRNAseq_scType_2026-10-26` subdirectory of this repository.

```{r step5_sctype_load, message = FALSE}

# Load scType functions from GitHub
source(file.path(params$sctype.fn_url, "gene_sets_prepare.R"))
source(file.path(params$sctype.fn_url, "sctype_score_.R"))

# Download the full database
db_url <- params$sctype.db_url
temp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
download.file(db_url, destfile = temp_file, mode = "wb")

# Read the database for immune system
db <- read.xlsx(temp_file)
db_immune <- db[db$tissueType == params$sctype.tissue, ]

# Prepare gene sets
gs_list <- gene_sets_prepare(temp_file, params$sctype.tissue)

cat("Available cell types in database:\n")
print(names(gs_list$gs_positive))
```

### Calculate and visualize scType scores

A quantile cutoff is applied to low-confidence clusters relative to the other clusters, so with 0.6 about 60% of clusters are labelled "Unknown" by construction. Change `params$sctype.unknown_quantile` if this is too aggressive.

```{r step6_sctype_score, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}

# Get scaled data
scaled_data <- as.matrix(LayerData(integrated_seurat, layer = "scale.data"))

# Calculate scores
es_max <- sctype_score(
  scRNAseqData = scaled_data,
  scaled = TRUE,
  gs = gs_list$gs_positive,
  gs2 = gs_list$gs_negative
)

# Assign cell types to clusters
clusters <- integrated_seurat@meta.data[[cluster.col]]
cL_results <- do.call("rbind", lapply(unique(clusters), function(cl) {
  es_max_cl <- sort(rowSums(es_max[, clusters == cl]), decreasing = TRUE)

  top_score <- es_max_cl[1]
  top_type <- names(es_max_cl)[1]

  data.frame(
    cluster = cl,
    type = top_type,
    scores = top_score,
    ncells = sum(clusters == cl)
  )
}))

# Filter low-confidence assignments
# NOTE: a quantile cutoff is relative to the other clusters, so with 0.6 about
# 60% of clusters are labelled "Unknown" by construction; lower
# params$sctype.unknown_quantile if that is too aggressive
score_threshold <- quantile(cL_results$scores, params$sctype.unknown_quantile)
cL_results$type[cL_results$scores < score_threshold] <- "Unknown"

# Create mapping and apply to cells
cluster_to_sctype <- setNames(cL_results$type, cL_results$cluster)
integrated_seurat$sctype_annotation <- unname(cluster_to_sctype[
  as.character(integrated_seurat@meta.data[[cluster.col]])
])

# Visualize
p_sctype <- DimPlot(
  integrated_seurat,
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  group.by = "sctype_annotation",
  label = TRUE,
  label.size = 4,
  pt.size = 0.1,
  repel = TRUE
) +
  ggtitle("scType: Marker-Based Annotation") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
print(p_sctype)

ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/automated_annotation/12_sctype_annotation.png"), p_sctype,
       width = 11, height = 8, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

# Save scType results
write.csv(cL_results, file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/sctype_cluster_scores.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## scCATCH: tissue-specific automated annotation

scCATCH finds cluster-specific marker genes and matches them to a curated
tissue-specific database (`cellmatch`).

```{r step7_sccatch, message = FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 14: scCATCH annotation
#-----------------------------------------------

sccatch_species <- c(human = "Human", mouse = "Mouse")[[params$species]]

# Prepare data for scCATCH
obj_sccatch <- createscCATCH(
  data = LayerData(integrated_seurat, layer = "data"),
  cluster = as.character(integrated_seurat@meta.data[[cluster.col]])
)

# Find marker genes for each cluster
obj_sccatch <- findmarkergene(
  object = obj_sccatch,
  species = sccatch_species,
  marker = cellmatch,
  tissue = params$sccatch.tissue,
  cancer = params$sccatch.cancer,
  cell_min_pct = params$sccatch.cell_min_pct,
  logfc = params$sccatch.logfc,
  pvalue = params$sccatch.pvalue
)

# Find cell types based on markers
obj_sccatch <- findcelltype(obj_sccatch)

# Extract results
sccatch_celltype <- obj_sccatch@celltype

# Create cluster to cell type mapping
cluster_to_sccatch <- setNames(
  sccatch_celltype$cell_type,
  sccatch_celltype$cluster
)

# Apply to all cells
integrated_seurat$sccatch_annotation <- unname(cluster_to_sccatch[
  as.character(integrated_seurat@meta.data[[cluster.col]])
])

# Handle unmapped clusters
integrated_seurat$sccatch_annotation[
  is.na(integrated_seurat$sccatch_annotation)
] <- "Unknown"

# Visualize
p_sccatch <- DimPlot(
  integrated_seurat,
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  group.by = "sccatch_annotation",
  label = TRUE,
  label.size = 4,
  pt.size = 0.1,
  repel = TRUE
) +
  ggtitle("scCATCH: Tissue-Specific Database") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
print(p_sccatch)

ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/automated_annotation/13_sccatch_annotation.png"), p_sccatch,
       width = 11, height = 8, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

# Save detailed results
write.csv(sccatch_celltype,
          file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/sccatch_cluster_assignments.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# Save marker evidence
marker_evidence <- obj_sccatch@markergene
write.csv(marker_evidence,
          file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/sccatch_marker_evidence.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```
